hook: Rates got the jitters. Buyers didn't.

items.headline: Geopolitics nudged rates up
items.line: Tension around Iran spooked the bond market, and mortgage rates ticked higher along with it.

items.headline: Buyers shrugged it off
items.line: Demand stayed positive anyway — a scary headline isn't the same as a scary house payment.

items.headline: New housing law: read the fine print
items.line: It's sold as buyer relief, but it's really a builder incentive — more homes later, not lower payments now.

caption:
Rates got a little jumpy this week — and honestly, not because of anything housing did. Global tension poked the bond market, so mortgage rates ticked up. The plot twist? Buyers didn't blink. Demand stayed steady, because a scary news headline isn't the same as a scary monthly payment. Meanwhile, that shiny "new housing law" making the rounds is less buyer-relief and more builder-incentive — great news, just on a longer timeline than the headlines suggest. Read the fine print like an underwriter and the story changes. 🍞
